announcements.name: groundcover's complete-state model
announcements.shortDescription: Agents reason over full system state rather than a curated slice, reducing hallucinated diagnoses
announcements.longDescription: groundcover proposes an architecture built for data abundance in which agents reason over complete system state rather than a curated slice or summary. The speaker argues that partial context is what creates hallucinated diagnoses, and that context quality matters as much as model quality, possibly more. This distinction separates an agent confidently hallucinating a fix from one that actually understands what is wrong.

announcements.name: Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC)
announcements.shortDescription: Telemetry stays inside the customer's own cloud for control, governance, and sensitive-data handling
announcements.longDescription: BYOC (Bring Your Own Cloud) is the first of groundcover's architectural bets, keeping everything inside the customer's own cloud. The speaker notes this matters for control, governance, and handling sensitive telemetry.

announcements.name: Zero instrumentation, zero friction
announcements.shortDescription: The observability layer instruments automatically because humans cannot keep instrumentation current in AI-generated systems
announcements.longDescription: Zero instrumentation and zero friction is groundcover's second architectural bet, where the observability layer instruments automatically. The speaker argues you cannot depend on humans to manually keep instrumentation current in AI-generated systems.

announcements.name: "Move the LLM up; push the analysis down"
announcements.shortDescription: The model handles intent and investigation strategy while the backend does deterministic analytical work close to the data
announcements.longDescription: This is a new observability model where the LLM is moved up and the analysis is pushed down, meaning the model is not the execution engine. The LLM's job is to understand intent, decide investigation strategy, generate deterministic operations, and interpret results, while the backend does the actual analytical work close to the data, accurately and cheaply. The goal is to have the model orchestrate investigation over a deterministic analytical system with complete telemetry rather than brute forcing analysis itself.
